categories.title: New Features
list: Flesh in the Physics tab is now a cage: a small shell fitted to the bone's mesh that swings as one lump about the bone's pivot, lags at its free end, keeps its volume, and that every vertex follows. A pair of bones, or one mesh that holds two parts, press on each other. Looks: pouch, seat, belly, thigh, jelly, soft flesh, firm flesh

New flesh controls: softness, firmness, meat (how heavy and fleshy it feels), reach, lag, settling of the swing and of the jiggle, turn about the base, volume, swell, the soft zone and the meshes that ride on it

Flesh works on a bone of cubes as it does on a mesh: the game cuts each cube face into a grid and moves that, and the preview does the same (a flat cube is left as it is, and cloth still needs a mesh)
The checker reads the flesh section the way the game does, names the keys of the old per-vertex flesh that no longer apply, and reads the old name of the section

The Physics panel is redone to sit in Blockbench: a toolbar with Simulate, Restart, Poke, Undo and Redo, collapsible sections, one slider and number box for every value, a bone list that can show only the bones with physics, and the type of a bone (spring, chain, cloth, flesh) picked from buttons that say why one is not available

Flesh now has every option the game reads: pair it with a second bone, choose whether the bones under it are soft or ride on it, the pivot (the bone, the cage or a point), the free end and the side it hangs from, how it is held, walking bounce and sway, how a pair squeezes, how it behaves under clothes, which of the model's bones press it, and an allow or deny list of bones. Values are written to the file only when they differ from the look

The Physics tab is now six windows, each a Blockbench panel that can be docked, floated or tabbed where you like, as in an editor: Physics (simulate and test motion), Bones (the hierarchy), Properties (type, looks and settings of the picked bones), Shapes (collision shapes), Test Objects, and JSON (the text the game reads, kept in step with every change, and editable with a check as you type)
Every slider has a small button that puts it back to its default (the default of the look it started from, or of the move), shown when it has been changed
When a bone cannot be picked for a list, the message and the tooltip of its greyed row say why (no geometry, above or below the part in the bone tree, shape switched off)

The camera can be held on the model, or on the picked bone, while it simulates, so the physics can be watched without a walk, a spin or a jump in the way; walking left and right, forward and back, going up and down and turning can each be switched off, and the camera goes back to where it was when the simulation stops
The collision shapes and the lines of springs, chains and flesh can be shown or hidden from two buttons on the toolbar of the Physics window, without opening Shapes

Fourteen test moves instead of six, each with settings of its own (distance, pace, direction, height, how hard it stops and so on): walk, run, turn, spin, jump, bounce, crouch, shake, walk in a circle, figure of eight, start and stop, knock and dance

Choosing bones is the same everywhere: lists of bones (the pieces that ride on a flesh or cloth, the bones it reacts to, a flesh's pair) are chips with one Pick bones button that takes clicks in the 3D view or in the Bones window, where the bones that cannot be picked for that list are greyed out and do nothing; the scrolling lists of ticks are gone

Settings are laid out for reading: the name and value on one line, the slider under it, and a description of what it does under that (the question mark in Properties hides the descriptions); each group says what it is for

Lists of bones (the pieces that ride on a flesh, the bones it reacts to, its pair) can be filled by clicking bones in the 3D view; the bones it reacts to is one list with ticks (all, none, invert) instead of two modes that meant the same thing

Pick several bones at once (ctrl-click in the list or the view, shift-click for a run of the list): the type, the look and every slider you change are changed on all of them, each keeping its own other values

Test shapes are objects: each has a position, a turn and a size, can be duplicated, and is moved, turned and scaled with the gizmo in the view (the move, rotate and scale tools); the gizmo follows a shape that sweeps and comes back if it was lost
A test shape can sweep along the axis you choose (X, Y or Z), as far and as fast as you set
Opening and closing a branch of the bone list shows at once
Cloth meshes of up to 2000 welded vertices are simulated by default (it was 600), so a dressed model's top is no longer left as modelled with a warning
A click in the view picks the bone of the cube or mesh under it, as in the Animate tab
Test shapes can be picked in the panel or the view and moved with the move gizmo in 3D; a bone and a test shape are never picked together

Simulated flesh and cloth keep the model's texture (a mesh keeps its own texture coordinates and materials; a bone of cubes is drawn as the grid the simulation moves, with the cubes' texture), and are shaded smoothly
A mesh that rides on a pair of flesh bones moves with the one of the pair nearest it only, as in the game

Flesh is pressed in by test shapes, the floor and the model's own shapes on the bones it is pressed by, with the volume pressed in swelling out elsewhere, so a dent can be seen without opening the game

categories.title: Changes
list: Flesh made for the old per-vertex solver keeps its entry; the numbers that no longer apply are dropped the first time its controls are edited
What presses on flesh in the game from outside the model (other models, players and blocks) is not drawn in the preview

categories.title: Strut Scenes
list: The workspace is now called Strut Scenes (File, New, Strut Scenes): a project type for making a scene, or the clips of one skeleton, for several characters on one timeline. It has no model of its own and no modelling tools (Animate mode only): the person making the scene only animates

Kinds of scene: a new scene asks what kind it is. A kind (a scene template) says who takes part, which skeleton each role needs, and which clips there are, how they are named, whether they loop, how long they may be, how many variants and sides they have. Two built-in kinds, a free scene and clips for one skeleton; a mod, a pack tool or another plugin adds its own (see docs/STRUT_SCENES_API.md)

The Scene panel is the whole scene in one place: each role is a row with an Add button until it has a character (from a preset or a file), each clip of the kind is a row that says what is missing and makes the next clip with one press, named and set as the kind says, with its phase, variant and side written into the layout for you. Check and Export are at its foot; a missing required role or clip, a wrong skeleton, loop mode or length stops the export and says so

Characters are loaded for you with their models and textures; show or hide, change who one is, give one another model of the same skeleton without losing a keyframe, or remove it. Where a character stands is its own move and turn in the viewport. Export writes each character's clips into its own clip set, made for its skeleton ID with its stage position folded into its root bone, and the scene's layout. The web version exports one zip

A scene is saved as a normal Blockbench project: characters, textures, keyframes and the kind of scene come back when it is opened. Sounds and particles are given to the first character. A timeline grouped by character and importing existing animations are not built yet

Guided tours: Help, Strut Toolkit Tour and Strut Scenes Tour light the part of the screen each step is about and explain it. Each is offered once, the first time a project of that kind is opened (Take the tour, Not now, or Do not ask again); either can be skipped at any step (Skip tour or Escape), stepped back and forward (Back, Next, the arrow keys), and played again from the Help menu or the ? in the Scene panel. The scenes tour can start a practice scene to follow along in
Character presets: folders of ready-made characters a tool registers once, so adding one is a single choice

The timeline of a scene is grouped by character: the rows of each character are kept together, under a heading with the character's name and a coloured band down their left edge, and a click on the heading folds the character's rows away or opens them again. Two characters' bones of the same name are told apart, and selecting bones in any order keeps the groups
The Variable Placeholders panel is hidden in a scene, which has no use for it; View, Strut Scenes: Show or Hide Variable Placeholders brings it back. Other projects keep their layout
A character's bones are picked by clicking its geometry in the viewport, as in any animation (the geometry was locked, which stopped clicks; scenes made before are unlocked when opened)

categories.title: Skeleton ID
list: A model project has a Skeleton ID in its properties (such as mymod:creature_a): a name for the rig the model is built on, written into the model file and into every animation file exported from the project. A scene only lets a model fill a role made for its skeleton ID, and an animation file that names one is matched by it instead of by the bone fingerprint
Importing animations made for a different skeleton ID than the project's says so. Files without one work as before

categories.title: Bug Fixes
list: Box selecting the UVs of a mesh no longer selects cubes that are not selected. With only a mesh selected in a box UV project, dragging a rectangle in the UV editor also selected every cube whose UV box lay under it, because the editor took the project's box UV setting for the answer when no cube was selected to ask. A mesh has face UVs, so the box selection now works on the selected elements only. With a cube selected, or nothing, nothing changes

categories.title: New Features
list: Export and import .strutmodel and .strutanim, meshes and armatures with skinning, controller-based animation with easings, Molang and event markers, armour sets and wearer profiles, and the Strut Physics tab
Opens older Bedrock-style .geo.json models and animations
